sections.en: S&P 500 is changing hands near $7,774, +0.66% over the past 24 hours and +0.91% on a 7-day view. Spot trades above the 50-day average ($7,643) and above the 200-day average ($7,267), keeping the medium-term structure constructive. The 30-day tape reads as a consolidation phase (+1.30%), suggesting the market is still rotating within a range.

sections.en:
**Trend structure.** Across horizons the picture is perfect bullish alignment (price > EMA20 > EMA50 > EMA200), the textbook configuration of a trend-following regime where pullbacks into the 20-day mean tend to be bought. Spot at $7,774 versus EMA20 $7,689, EMA50 $7,643 and EMA200 $7,267 frames the medium-term bias mechanically rather than emotionally. From this configuration the desk's working assumption is that trend-following exposure is only justified while price holds the side of the 50-day average it currently occupies.

**Key levels.** The operational map reads: initial support at $7,765 (recent swing low); the lower Bollinger band $7,553 as the 2σ downside envelope; first resistance at $7,786 (recent swing high); upper band $7,793 as the stretch target. Levels derived from the last ~60 sessions of closes are guides for location, not promises of reaction; they mark where prior two-way business was done and therefore where resting liquidity is most plausible. ATR(14) of $67.91 implies a typical daily range of roughly 0.9 percent of spot, which is the unit of risk to size positions against.

**Momentum.** RSI(14) prints 59.0 — neutral territory; MACD (12/26/9) sits above its signal line (17.18 vs 12.33, histogram +4.841), consistent with building momentum. Momentum readings are state descriptors, not trade signals on their own; the desk treats confluence between momentum and level location as the actionable unit.

**Volatility & liquidity.** 30-day realized volatility annualizes near 12%; the 20-day band spans 3% of the mid — compressed, which often precedes a volatility expansion; 7-day turnover runs at 1.03x the trailing-month norm. Behavior around these regimes — absorption at band edges, volume confirmation on breaks — is what separates a tradeable move from noise.

**Performance context.** On longer windows the asset has returned +1.30% over 30 days and +3.37% over 90 days. Positioning decisions made on monthly horizons should respect these base rates instead of extrapolating the last week. The 7-session change (+0.91%) is the shortest window the desk treats as signal rather than noise.

sections.en:
**Bullish scenario.** Continuation higher requires acceptance above $7,786 on expanding turnover; continued holds of the 50-day average ($7,643). Under those conditions the path of least resistance flips to buy-the-dip, with prior resistance converting to support as the confirmation test.

**Bearish scenario.** Downside continuation triggers on a decisive loss of $7,765. In that case failed support typically becomes the new ceiling, and momentum chasers provide the exit liquidity.

Net take on S&P 500: spot $7,774 with the medium-term bias constructive while price holds the relevant side of the 50-day average. The 24-hour tape (+0.66%) is consistent with that bias. Decision zones are the levels named in the technical section, not opinions: trade the reaction at those prices, not the headline of the day.
